_doc: Engine verification suites. Read by scripts/verify/plan.py (CI planning, change detection) and scripts/verify/run.sh (local and CI runs). Fields: cargo = the cargo target selection that builds the suite; test = optional exact test name inside that binary; platforms = where each tier runs it (platform-independent logic runs on linux only); roots = workspace packages whose dependency closure decides whether a change can affect the suite; own = files that only affect this suite (a change confined to them selects just this suite). skip = case-id globs left out of a tier on a platform (CAP_VERIFY_SKIP), to keep the FAST tier within its time budget; the FULL tier runs them. Exception: CI Windows VMs (Blacksmith windows-2025, formerly hosted windows-2022) have no D3D11 video device, so every Windows case decodes with FFmpeg (the code Linux runs) and renders on the WARP software rasterizer; on hosted windows-2022 the 120 s jitter-camera export and playback and the 3000-seek storms took 6 to more than 15 minutes each (killed at the 15 minute per-test limit in 4 of 5 full runs), so FULL leaves them to Linux and macOS. cases = the executed-case floor per tier and platform: the gate fails when fewer distinct cases whose id starts with prefix ran across all shards (scripts/verify/floor.py). unsupported = per-platform case globs that may report unsupported (with the reason); CI sets CAP_VERIFY_REQUIRE_SUPPORTED=1, so any other unsupported case fails.

suites.name: verify-self
suites.about: marker codecs, reference timeline model, oracle and report self-tests

suites.name: export
suites.about: every exported frame against the reference model (MP4, GIF, both decoders on macOS)

suites.name: playback
suites.about: offline-driven editor playback frames against the reference model

suites.name: seek
suites.about: random, keyframe and scrub seeks against the reference model

suites.name: crash
suites.about: crash safety of fragmented Studio recording: in-process vs out-of-process muxer equality, recorder and muxer kills, recovery against what is physically on disk (needs the cap-muxer binary, built by run.sh)

suites.name: chaos
suites.about: chaos and resilience: hostile device data, files, projects and settings through the recording, editor, playback, export and recovery engines, each probe in a child process so panics, aborts, signals, Objective-C exceptions and hangs are classified (needs the cap-muxer binary, built by run.sh)

suites.name: audio
suites.about: export and offline playback audio against sample-accurate markers (mic, system audio, cuts, speeds, mute, volume, A/V offset)

suites.name: editing
suites.about: random edit sequences (split, delete, speed, trim, reorder, transitions) exported and checked frame by frame against the reference model

suites.name: captions
suites.about: fake-transcriber captions: caption segments and rendered captions on the right frames

suites.name: decoder-model-ffmpeg
suites.about: model-based fuzzing of the FFmpeg decoder's request decisions on scripted media

suites.name: decoder-model-avf
suites.about: model-based fuzzing of the AVAssetReader decoder's request decisions on scripted media

suites.name: native-rendering
suites.about: native macOS rendering regressions (IOSurface source lifetime in the YUV converter)

windows.*/mf: Media Foundation decoding needs a D3D11 device with video support; CI Windows VMs render on the WARP software adapter, which has none, so the product falls back to FFmpeg there. Media Foundation is not exercised by CI.

recording._doc: Real capture (verify-recording.yml): distinct case ids each runner must record per tier (crates/verify/tests/recording.rs specs; system-only reports unsupported when the stimulus is silent).

macos-vt._doc: macOS MP4 exports on the VideoToolbox hardware H.264 encoder. Blacksmith macOS VMs have none: Cap opens h264_videotoolbox with allow_sw=0 for exports, which fails there ("Try -allow_sw 1", probe run 38853844860), so Cap falls back to libx264, a path real Macs only take when the hardware encoder is busy or over capacity. The suites that encode (export, audio) run again on hosted macOS when a change reaches encoding (encoders, export, the renderer's output and RGBA to NV12 conversion, media and frame conversion) or the suite itself, and in every full run (nightly, dispatch).
